questions.question: What is the Same-Origin Policy and CORS? How do they work?
questions.title: Same-Origin Policy & CORS Explained — Access-Control Headers
questions.direct_answer:
What is the Same-Origin Policy and CORS? How do they work?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** SOP blocks cross-origin reads by default; CORS relaxes with server-sent Access-Control-Allow-* headers; preflight for non-simple requests.

**Classic weak answer:** Thinking 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' is safe everywhere — it disables credential sending and fails for private data.

**Senior finish:** Walk through simple vs preflighted requests, credentials mode (include/same-origin/omit), and the common 'no CORS header' error debugging.

sections.title: Why this question matters
sections.content:
This question — **Same-Origin Policy & CORS Explained — Access-Control Headers** — shows up constantly in **frontend / fullstack** interviews because it separates candidates who memorized docs from candidates who can **reason about real systems**.

**Restate the prompt:** What is the Same-Origin Policy and CORS? How do they work?

A gold-level answer does four things in order:

1. **Define** the terms in plain English (what it is / what problem it solves).
2. **Explain the mechanism** (what runs when: browser, bundler, framework, network).
3. **Compare trade-offs** (speed vs correctness vs security vs DX) with **when you would not use** the default.
4. **Ground it in production** — caching, auth, observability, tests, or an incident you handled.

Interviewers are listening for: **SOP blocks cross-origin reads by default; CORS relaxes with server-sent Access-Control-Allow-* headers; preflight for non-simple requests**.

The fastest way to lose points is: **Thinking 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' is safe everywhere — it disables credential sending and fails for private data**.

If you only add one “senior” layer, make it: **Walk through simple vs preflighted requests, credentials mode (include/same-origin/omit), and the common 'no CORS header' error debugging**.

sections.title: Deep dive — what to say
sections.content:
### What to explain (middle of the answer)

- **Core mechanics:** SOP blocks cross-origin reads by default; CORS relaxes with server-sent Access-Control-Allow-* headers; preflight for non-simple requests
- **Concrete shape:** give a small code or config snippet *only if it clarifies* (5–15 lines max).
- **Interviewer follow-ups:** expect “what breaks in production?”, “how do you debug?”, “what would you measure?” — answer them proactively.

### How to sound senior (without rambling)

- Tie the feature to **user-visible outcomes** (performance, accessibility, security).
- Mention **one failure mode** you have actually seen (race, stale cache, hydration mismatch, flaky test).
- Close with **one decision rule** (“choose X when …; choose Y when …”).

sections.title: Trade-offs & senior signal
sections.content:
### Trade-offs interviewers expect you to name

- **Speed vs safety** (types, runtime checks, validation).
- **DX vs constraints** (framework magic vs explicit wiring).
- **SEO / first paint vs interactivity** (SSR/SSG/CSR choices where relevant).
- **Security vs convenience** (tokens, cookies, localStorage, third-party scripts).

### What “book answer” misses

- **Book answer:** repeats definitions.
- **Strong answer:** names **thinking 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' is safe everywhere — it disables credential sending and fails for private data** and what you do instead.

sections.title: How to answer verbally (timed)
sections.content:
**Open (15–20 seconds):** Restate the question and give the one-sentence definition.

**Body (45–60 seconds):** Walk through **SOP blocks cross-origin reads by default; CORS relaxes with server-sent Access-Control-Allow-* headers; preflight for non-simple requests** as a story: what runs, what breaks, what you log/measure.

**Pitfall (15 seconds):** Call out **Thinking 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *' is safe everywhere — it disables credential sending and fails for private data** — interviewers reward honesty about real bugs.

**Finish (15–20 seconds):** Add **Walk through simple vs preflighted requests, credentials mode (include/same-origin/omit), and the common 'no CORS header' error debugging**, then offer a trade-off question back (“do you optimize for TTFB or TTI here?”).

questions.question: What is a CORS preflight (OPTIONS) request? When is it triggered?
questions.title: CORS Preflight OPTIONS Request — When & Why It's Triggered
questions.direct_answer:
What is a CORS preflight (OPTIONS) request? When is it triggered?

**In one line:** name the mechanism, where it applies (the browser pipeline, framework hooks, and user-visible outcomes), and the user-visible outcome.

**Interviewers dig into:** OPTIONS sent before non-simple requests (custom headers, PUT/DELETE/PATCH, non-simple content-type); Access-Control-Max-Age caches the preflight.

**Classic weak answer:** Adding a custom Authorization header and not allowing it in Access-Control-Allow-Headers, causing the preflight to fail silently.

**Senior finish:** List what makes a request 'simple' vs preflighted per the Fetch spec, and how Access-Control-Max-Age reduces preflight traffic.
